newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hoechst sees 97 adjusted profit rising.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst sees 97 adjusted profit rising.

text.p: German chemicals group Hoechst AG said on Monday it expected its operating earnings to rise on an adjusted basis this year but sales would drop to between 42 billion and 47 billion marks due to the spin-off of three units.
"In operating business, Hoechst expects a rise in comparable earnings in 1997 amid lively demand, rising prices in the industrial sector and favourable currency effects," Hoechst said in a statement.

The company said its operating earnings dropped 22 percent to 1.03 billion marks in the first quarter, but that this represented a rise of 20 percent after adjustment to take into account special factors.
Group pre-tax profit rose nine percent to 831 million marks, also calculated on an adjusted basis.
Hoechst said it had adjusted the earnings comparison to reflect that restructuring costs in the first quarter of 1997 were sharply higher than the first quarter of 1996.
Hoechst said the first quarter of 1997 contained 195 million marks in restructuring costs which were 110 million marks higher than in the year-earlier period.

In addition, the first quarter of 1996 contained 300 million marks income from the sale of Hoechst's printing plate business and a 85 million mark profit contribution from SGL Carbon in which Hoechst no longer has a majority stake.
Hoechst said sales in 1997 would fall from last year's level of 50.9 billion marks because it had spun off its special chemicals, plastics and diagnostics divisions.
Looking ahead to the full-year results, Hoechst said, "Overall, the profit will be lower than in the previous year due to smaller extraordinary income."

Hoechst said its drugs business went well in most business segments and regions during the first quarter and that the integration of its unit Hoechst Marion Roussel was running according to plan. --Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525
